newsitem.title: UK: BRITISH TOP THE EUROPEAN CHOCOHOLICS LEAGUE.
newsitem.headline: BRITISH TOP THE EUROPEAN CHOCOHOLICS LEAGUE.

text.p: The British are Europe's largest consumers of chocolate, spending an average of $91.11 per person each year, according to a new market report.

Market research group Datamonitor said on Monday that the European chocolate market is worth about $18 billion annually, up from $16.84 billion in 1992. The total European confectionary market is worth about $30 billion.

The British chocolate market is the biggest in Europe at $5.32 billion a year, up from $4.45 billion in 1992. Germany is the second largest market at $4.27 billion a year, though per capita spending is only $52.01, Datamonitor said.
The Irish are the second biggest consumers of chocolate, spending an average of $90.39 each per year, with the Swedish in third place at $88.19 a year.
Despite the high reputation of Swiss chocolate, the Swiss rank only eighth, spending an average of $64.57 each per year, Datamonitor said.
Trailing the 16 European countries is Spain, with average chocolate spending of $11.64, Datamonitor said.
